prompt: Can you list the channels our workspace admin named Robert belongs to, and confirm that he's actually flagged as admin rather than just a regular member?
binding_note: Workspace admin role is the identifying join, not a fact reported after the fact: filtering users by admin role in user_teams narrows the pool to three people, and filtering those by the first name 'Robert' leaves two distinct admins (Robert Walsh and Robert Kim) with disjoint channel-membership sets, so which conversation-membership records are intended stays unresolved.

roles.facts: real_name Robert Walsh, username robertwalsh, member of workspace T01WORKSPACE
roles.reason: First candidate matching both the name condition and the admin workspace-role condition

roles.facts: new user real_name Robert Kim, username robert.kim, email robertk@neuroflow.ai, member of workspace T01WORKSPACE
roles.reason: Second candidate matching both the name condition and the admin workspace-role condition; added to realize genuine ambiguity under the assigned route

roles.facts: Robert Walsh's user_teams row carries role=admin
roles.reason: Workspace-membership role that identifies Robert Walsh as an eligible admin along the assigned route

roles.facts: new user_teams row for Robert Kim carries role=admin
roles.reason: Workspace-membership role that identifies Robert Kim as an eligible admin along the assigned route

roles.facts: Robert Walsh holds conversation memberships in general, random, and engineering
roles.reason: Candidate conversation-membership set if the intended admin Robert is Robert Walsh

roles.facts: new conversation memberships for Robert Kim in product-growth and frontend
roles.reason: Candidate conversation-membership set if the intended admin Robert is Robert Kim

roles.facts: Morgan Freeman's user_teams row carries role=admin
roles.reason: Satisfies the admin-role condition but fails the name condition ('Robert'), so his channel memberships are excluded

roles.facts: Robert Chen's user_teams row carries role=member
roles.reason: Satisfies the name condition but fails the admin-role condition, so his channel memberships are excluded

roles.facts: Hubert Marek's user_teams row carries role=member
roles.reason: Fails both the name and the admin-role condition

roles.facts: Robert Chen holds conversation memberships in project-alpha-dev, core-infra, model-research, product-growth, and frontend
roles.reason: Named Robert but his workspace role is member, not admin, so these memberships are excluded by the role condition

obligations.name: admin_robert_channel_memberships
obligations.description: Conversation memberships held by whichever workspace-admin user named Robert is intended; two disjoint candidate sets exist (Robert Walsh's and Robert Kim's) since the admin-role filter narrows the pool but the name still leaves two matches.
obligations.scope: conversation memberships of the workspace-admin user named Robert

obligations.name: admin_robert_workspace_role
obligations.description: The workspace membership role of the same candidate Robert, confirming admin status as displayed alongside the selected memberships (not used to further disambiguate between the two Roberts).
obligations.scope: workspace membership role of the workspace-admin user named Robert

task_spec.text: List the channels our workspace admin named Robert belongs to, and confirm his admin status.

access_plan: Use users.list to enumerate workspace users and their real_name fields to find those named Robert, then check each candidate's workspace role (admin vs member) via team membership info; for each candidate whose role is admin, use users.conversations (or channel_members lookups) to enumerate the channels they belong to.
